answer.evidence: The layer-1 weights look like a uniform initialisation bounded at roughly ±81 integer units (1/sqrt(576) ≈ 0.0417, and 0.0417 / 0.000515 ≈ 81). Values outside that range must therefore come from training, so I used them to locate learned structure. Units 4, 5, 6, 13, 14, 15, 19 and 24 stay within that bound and appear essentially untrained. The trained units fall into three kinds of patterns, none of them a compact patch. (1) Centre-positive, surround-negative units. Unit 20 has large positives in rows 8-16, columns 6-16 (99, 96, 92, 91, 90, 88). Its large negatives sit on the periphery (row 2 about -92, -89, -91; row 3 -95, -90; row 22 mean about -32). Units 18 and 29 also concentrate their large positives in the central rows 7-17. (2) Surround-positive, centre-negative units. Unit 17 has edge rows 2-4 and 22-23, plus the right column, at +85 to +96, and central rows 8-15 at -88 to -95. Unit 23 has top rows 0-3 and the left column positive, with centre values of -86 and -87. Unit 26 shows the same peripheral-positive, centre-negative pattern. (3) Broad brightness or darkness units with no spatial focus: units 1, 2, 8, 10 and 27 positive; units 3, 7, 11, 12, 16, 21, 22, 25, 28, 30 and 31 negative. I scanned all four corner 3x3 blocks and the edge rows of every unit and found no small block of consistently extreme same-sign weights. Such a block is what a fixed marker, text or other non-anatomical artifact would leave behind. Through the rough pathway, treating every layer-2 unit as active, which is only an approximation since layer-2 ReLU gating is ignored: the centre detector unit 20 contributes about +7500 (malignant). The surround detectors contribute negatively: unit 26 about -14700 with its high always-on bias, unit 23 about -3200, unit 17 about -700. This is consistent with a genuine nodule-versus-surroundings contrast feature, not an artifact. Unit 23's top-row band and unit 17's bottom-row band are the most suspicious structures. However, they belong to symmetric peripheral rings, not isolated patches, and their net output effect is weak. I therefore do not call them a shortcut, which leaves some residual uncertainty.
answer.main_feature: The model contrasts bright tissue in the central region (nodule size and density, via centre-positive units such as 20, 18 and 29, which push toward malignant) against brightness in the surrounding periphery (via ring-shaped units 26, 23 and 17, which push toward benign). In effect, larger and denser central nodules relative to their surroundings score as malignant.
